subject: Expenditure corridor qualification & PO thresholds — follow-up from today's call
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@wavefin.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Expenditure corridor qualification & PO thresholds — follow-up from today's call

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + a couple homework items so we can size the right pilot/commit path: 

Call recap (2 min):
- WaveFin is planning a search-surface + summary assistant pilot (3 app endpoints) for Q3.
- Expected peak concurrent sessions: small (5–10), expected monthly tokens ~2–6M depending on retention depth.
- Primary procurement constraint: finance requires POs above $50k; anything under that can be handled as a credit card/contract route.

Questions / asks (so we can recommend an optimal unit econ):
1) Can you confirm the target monthly spend band you have in mind for the pilot? (e.g., <$10k, $10–50k, $50–150k).
2) For underwriting: what is your PO threshold (you mentioned ~$50k) and is there flexibility for an initial pilot to be invoiced?
3) Unit-econ target: what would be a comfortable $/1M token price for WaveFin if we guarantee a short committed slab?

Proposed next steps:
- I can send a short SOW + estimated spend scenarios at 3 price points ($1k/$900/$700 per 1M tokens) so you can run numbers against product metrics.
- If procurement needs a PDF of our pilot pricing and PO path, I can include a one-page procurement note.

I’ve copied Connor and Karthik so they can confirm pricing levers on our side and suggest an internal proposal that maps to your PO gating.

Thanks — available after 1pm PT if you'd like a quick follow-up.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0182
attachments: redwood-pilot-sow-v1.pdf (draft), procurement-one-pager.docx

From: Daniel Park <daniel@wavefin.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expenditure corridor qualification & PO thresholds — follow-up from today's call

Thanks Tessa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Pilot budget band: we're comfortable with $10–50k for an initial month-long pilot. If results look good, finance will sign up for a higher committed band.
2) PO threshold: our procurement team requires a PO for any invoice > $35k. We can accept an invoice under $35k without a formal PO. The $50k figure I mentioned earlier was a conservative upper bound.
3) Unit-econ target: for this use case we'd aim for <= $800 / 1M tokens — anything under that makes the pilot much easier to justify to the product team.

Attached is our internal procurement policy (redacted) so you see how approvals flow.

If you can send the SOW + 2–3 pricing scenarios (including a committed slab price and a month-to-month price), we’ll run it past procurement and get back within 48 hours.

Thanks — Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Product, WaveFin
D: (212) 555-0137
attachments: wavefin-procurement-policy.pdf

Tessa — forwarding Daniel's note. A couple internal points for the pricing scenarios I recommend we include: 

- Month-to-month (no commit): $1,200 / 1M tokens (baseline hosted price for this workload profile).
- 3-month pilot commit (soft commit, cancellable): $900 / 1M tokens, up to 10M tokens/month slab.
- 6-month reserved slab (hard commit): $700 / 1M tokens, minimum 6M tokens/month.

Additional notes: 
- We can build a PO-friendly invoice template; if WaveFin can accept an initial invoice under $35k for the first month, procurement can approve faster and procurement will process the PO for month two if they move forward.
- Call out latency/throughput SLOs in the SOW so product/procurement sees technical guardrails.

Karthik — can you confirm SLO language and if we should include a 7-day rollback window on reserved slabs?

Connor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@wavefin.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Expenditure corridor qualification & PO thresholds — follow-up from today's call

Thanks Daniel — appreciate the clear bands. Next steps from our side (I’ve attached a draft SOW and a one-page procurement note):

1) Draft SOW (attached): outlines a 1-month pilot with optional month-to-month continuation. Pricing scenarios included:
   - Month-to-month: $1,200 / 1M tokens (no commit)
   - 3-month soft commit: $900 / 1M tokens (up to 10M tokens/month slab)
   - 6-month reserved: $700 / 1M tokens (min 6M tokens/month)

2) Procurement note (attached): explains invoice routing, PO timing, and a sample invoice that keeps the first invoice < $35k to avoid immediate PO requirement.

3) Ask: Please confirm which pricing scenario you'd like us to price into the SOW so procurement can review. If you want, Connor can hop on a 20-min call with your procurement on Wed/Thu to walk them through the invoice/PO flow.

If you confirm "3-month soft commit @ $900/1M" or "month-to-month @ $1,200/1M" by end of day Thursday, we’ll push a DocuSign-ready SOW for signature and prepare the pilot environment.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting WaveFin live.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
